en.headline: Technical skills. No hype.
en.intro: A quick view of my working strengths, current limits and where I use AI. Select any skill to inspect how I work, what I would trust in production and the evidence behind it.
en.note: How I use AI: mostly as a speed multiplier, second opinion, or a way to find reasoning gaps faster. Where I depend on it heavily, I say so. If I cannot explain and verify a change, it belongs in the lab first.
en.legend:
Rating

Visible 0–10 self-rating

Not a certification score. A range indicates uncertainty; early-stage, AI-guided skills are deliberately not rated.

Independence

What I actually rely on

Memory, documentation, search or AI. Generated output only counts after I understand and verify it.

Production

How cautious I would be

Independent, review-first, sandbox-first or lab-only depending on the technology.

items.skill: Linux & shellServices, users, permissions, logs, packages, systemd, troubleshooting.
items.rating: 9/10■■■■■■■■■□very strong
items.assist: Independent day to day; documentation for uncommon flags or tools I have not used in a while.
items.production: Independent for familiar changes; verify before and after.

items.skill: NetworkingRouting, NAT, DNS, firewalling, private access and VPN paths.
items.rating: 8/10■■■■■■■■□□strong
items.assist: Very comfortable with the networks I actually run; docs/AI mainly for edge cases and design checks.
items.production: Independent on familiar topologies; review-first for more complex VLAN/switching designs.

items.skill: Docker / ComposeCompose files, logs, mounts, networking, health checks and recovery.
items.rating: 9/10■■■■■■■■■□very strong
items.assist: I can write, edit and reason about Compose files myself; docs/search when useful.
items.evidence: Operational configs are partly private by design.

items.skill: Kubernetes / Talos LinuxPrivate cluster with three control-plane/etcd nodes on Talos Linux, AMD64/ARM64 workloads, K3s migration, kubectl, ingress, storage and rollout checks.
items.rating: 4/10■■■■□□□□□□learning in practice
items.assist: Active lab practice with Kustomize, SOPS/age, service migration and data-restore checks. Setup and many changes remain heavily AI-assisted; I check the result on the running systems.
items.production: Lab/sandbox first. Three etcd voters and a controlled node restart are verified; application HA, recurring data backups and broader failure testing are not implied.
items.evidence:
CKA practice ↗
Talos operational configuration and migration evidence remain private.

items.skill: Proxmox VEVM lifecycle, templates, networking, lab systems and virtualization concepts.
items.rating: 7/10■■■■■■■□□□confident
items.assist: Strong virtualization understanding; I can operate Proxmox without AI while product-specific depth is still growing.
items.production: Independent for normal VM/lab work; review complex storage/network changes.

items.skill: Terraform / OpenTofuUsed for infrastructure definitions in my lab.
items.rating: Not ratedLimited hands-on, AI-guided
items.assist: I work with it while AI currently guides most authoring. I inspect the configuration and plan, run it, and validate the result rather than treating generated code as independent skill.

items.skill: AnsibleInventories, roles, bootstrap and configuration concepts used in lab work.
items.rating: Not ratedLimited hands-on, AI-guided
items.assist: I have worked with and use Ansible, but AI still guides most implementation. I review what it produces and validate the run instead of claiming independent authoring.

items.skill: SMB / NASShares, permissions, migrations and practical storage administration.
items.rating: 9/10■■■■■■■■■□very strong
items.assist: Mostly independent; little AI needed for normal administration.

items.skill: NFSMounts, Kubernetes storage paths, backups and service integration.
items.rating: 6/10■■■■■■□□□□working knowledge
items.assist: Newer area; comfortable with what I run, while unfamiliar behavior still sends me to docs/search.

items.skill: Prometheus / GrafanaBasic setup, dashboards, exporters, probes and troubleshooting.
items.rating: 4/10■■■■□□□□□□basic practical use
items.assist: I can set up the basics manually; for deeper tuning I am still learning and experimenting with AI assistance.

items.skill: NetBird / VPN / private networkingPeers, routes, access rules and private administration paths.
items.rating: 9/10■■■■■■■■■□very strong
items.assist: I can build routing and rules myself; AI mainly accelerates reasoning or catches logic holes.

items.skill: Git / GitHub ActionsRepos, diffs, CI checks, branch/PR flow and deployment workflows.
items.rating: 5–6/10comfortable basics
items.assist: Comfortable with normal workflows; docs/search for less common Git and Actions behavior.
items.evidence: This site's Actions ↗

items.skill: Bash / scriptingOperational helpers, pipelines, diagnostics and glue scripts.
items.rating: 9/10■■■■■■■■■□very strong
items.assist: Similar to Linux: strong daily use; docs for uncommon flags or syntax I have not touched in a while.
items.production: Independent for familiar scripts; always review anything destructive.

en.footer: These ratings are my own assessments, not generated scores. They are meant to make strengths and limits visible instead of hiding both behind a long technology list.

de.intro: Ein schneller Überblick über meine Praxis, Grenzen und meinen KI-Einsatz. Skill öffnen: Arbeitsweise, produktive Verantwortung und echte Nachweise.
de.note: Wie ich KI nutze: meistens als Beschleuniger, zweite Meinung oder um Denkfehler schneller zu finden. Wo ich stark davon abhängig bin, steht es auch so da. Wenn ich eine Änderung nicht erklären und prüfen kann, gehört sie zuerst ins Lab.
de.legend:
Rating

Sichtbare 0–10-Selbsteinschätzung

Kein Zertifikatsscore. Ein Bereich zeigt Unsicherheit; Skills mit wenig Praxis und starker KI-Führung bleiben bewusst ohne Zahlenwert.

Eigenständigkeit

Worauf ich wirklich zurückgreife

Gedächtnis, Doku, Suche oder KI. Generierter Output zählt erst, wenn ich ihn verstehe und geprüft habe.

Produktiv

Wie vorsichtig ich wäre

Selbstständig, Review zuerst, Sandbox zuerst oder nur Lab – je nach Technologie.
